purpose: Reference answers for cosine scoring of the self-recorded explanations (research/asr/self_recordings.py). Written before any recording exists, in plain textbook style, 80-120 words each.

answers.normalisation: Database normalisation is the process of organising the tables and columns of a relational database to reduce redundant data. Storing the same fact in several rows causes update, insertion and deletion anomalies, where changing or removing data in one place leaves the database inconsistent. Normalisation avoids these problems by decomposing large tables into smaller related tables linked by primary and foreign keys, without losing information, so the original data can be rebuilt with joins. The process follows normal forms based on functional dependencies: first normal form requires atomic values, second normal form removes partial dependencies on a composite key, and third normal form removes transitive dependencies. Highly normalised designs need more joins, so some systems denormalise for faster reads.
answers.deadlock: A deadlock is a situation in which a set of processes or threads are each waiting for a resource held by another member of the set, so none can continue. A deadlock can occur only when four conditions hold simultaneously: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait. For example, if thread A holds lock 1 and waits for lock 2 while thread B holds lock 2 and waits for lock 1, both wait forever. Deadlocks can be prevented by making one condition impossible, such as acquiring locks in a fixed order. Alternatively, a system can avoid unsafe states with the Banker's algorithm, or detect cycles in a wait-for graph and recover by aborting a process.
answers.tcp-vs-udp: TCP and UDP are transport-layer protocols that run on top of IP and use port numbers to deliver data to applications. TCP is connection-oriented: a three-way handshake sets up a connection, and sequence numbers, acknowledgements and retransmission provide reliable, ordered delivery. TCP also performs flow control and congestion control. UDP is connectionless and best-effort: it sends independent datagrams with no guarantee of delivery or order and no congestion control. Because UDP has a smaller header and no handshake or retransmission delays, it has lower overhead and latency. TCP is therefore used for web pages, email and file transfer, while UDP suits DNS lookups, live audio and video, voice calls and online games.
answers.overfitting: Overfitting happens when a machine-learning model learns the training data too closely, including its noise and random details, instead of the general pattern. An overfitted model performs very well on the training data but worse on new, unseen data, so it generalises poorly. Common causes are a model too complex for the amount of data, too little or noisy training data, and training for too long. Overfitting is detected by comparing training error with error on a held-out validation set, or by cross-validation. It can be reduced with more data, a simpler model, regularisation such as L2 penalties or dropout, and early stopping. Underfitting is the opposite problem: a model too simple to fit even the training data.
answers.virtual-memory: Virtual memory is a memory-management technique that gives each process its own large, private address space, independent of the size and layout of physical RAM. The memory management unit translates virtual addresses into physical addresses using page tables maintained by the operating system, and a translation lookaside buffer caches recent translations. Memory is divided into fixed-size pages, and only the pages a process is using need to be in RAM; the rest can be kept on disk. When a process accesses a page that is not in memory, a page fault occurs and the operating system loads the page, evicting another one if necessary. Virtual memory isolates processes and lets programs larger than RAM run, but excessive paging causes thrashing.
answers.process-vs-thread: A process is a program in execution with its own private address space and resources, such as memory and open files, and the operating system isolates processes from one another. A thread is a unit of execution scheduled by the operating system inside a process, and one process can contain several threads. Threads of the same process share its code, global data, heap and open files, but each thread has its own stack, registers and program counter. Because threads share memory, they communicate easily but need synchronisation, such as locks, to avoid race conditions. Processes communicate through inter-process communication, such as pipes or sockets. Creating and switching threads is cheaper than for processes because no new address space is needed.
